tools.name: agent_flow_runs_event
tools.desc: Append a progress event to a run and push it to anyone watching the portal live. Types: node.status (with status started|finished|failed|skipped and a nodeId), run.waiting (parked on a human node), note (free text), run.finished (with status succeeded|failed|abandoned). Include model/inputTokens/outputTokens/durationMs on a finished node so the canvas can show cost per step. summary is capped at 2KB.

tools.name: agent_flow_runs_start
tools.desc: Open an execution of a Workflow Designer flow and return its runId. Snapshots the flow graph onto the run so the execution stays readable even if the flow is edited later. Report progress with agent_flow_runs_event. For a sub-flow handoff, pass the calling run as parentRunId and the calling node as parentNodeId.

tools.name: agent_flows_get
tools.desc: Get one Workflow Designer flow including its full node/edge graph. Node data carries agentType (a .claude/agents persona slug), model, prompt, entryPoint, fanOut ('all' = run every outgoing branch, 'one' = take exactly one), and for human nodes assigneeIds (project-member user ids who must sign off). Edge kind is handoff or dependency.

tools.name: agent_flows_list
tools.desc: List the Workflow Designer agent flows attached to a project. Returns a slim row per flow (no graph payload) — call agent_flows_get for the graph itself.

tools.name: ai_conversations_get
tools.desc: Fetch a conversation + full message history. Useful for auditing what the in-app AI assistant has been doing.

tools.name: ai_conversations_list
tools.desc: List AI chat conversations for this client (in-app portal AI assistant history).

tools.name: ai_credits_balance
tools.desc: Return current AI token balance, monthly grant, and pay-as-you-go status.

tools.name: ai_credits_ledger
tools.desc: Recent credit ledger entries (grants, usage, purchases, refunds) with running balances.

tools.name: approvals_approve
tools.desc: Apply a pending MCP-staged write. Re-runs the original mutation with the stored payload, marks status=applied. If the apply fails, marks status=failed with errorMessage.

args.name: note
args.desc: Optional review note recorded on the change.

tools.name: approvals_get
tools.desc: Full detail of a pending change including payload and original snapshot (for review).

tools.name: approvals_list
tools.desc: List staged MCP writes awaiting review. Filter by status or entity type.

tools.name: approvals_reject
tools.desc: Mark a pending change as rejected. The staged mutation is NOT applied.

args.name: note
args.desc: Reason shown to the original submitter.

tools.name: automations_create
tools.desc: Define a new automation rule. Trigger = { event: string, ...metadata }; conditions = [{ field, operator, value }]; actions = [{ tool: string, params: object }]. Rule starts enabled.

args.name: trigger
args.desc: { event: "email.campaign.sent", ... }

tools.name: automations_delete
tools.desc: Permanently delete an automation rule. Logs are retained.

tools.name: automations_list
tools.desc: List automation rules configured for the client, including trigger + condition + action blobs.

tools.name: automations_toggle
tools.desc: Flip the `enabled` flag on an automation rule without touching its trigger/conditions/actions.

tools.name: automations_update
tools.desc: Update name, description, trigger, conditions, actions, or productScope. Use automations_toggle for just the enabled flag.

tools.name: block_templates_create
tools.desc: Create a reusable CMS block template. Writes a base row with everything staged in the `draft` jsonb (pendingCreate=true). The template picker and "use this template" flow ignore draft-only templates until `block_templates_publish` is called. `slug` must be unique across the agency. `scope: "global"` syncs the template back to every post that embeds it; `block` and `section` are copy-on-insert.

args.name: lockedFields
args.desc: Field paths that can't be edited when the template is reused (e.g. "0.type", "0.style.backgroundColor").

tools.name: block_templates_delete
tools.desc: Stages a tombstone on the template (draft.pendingDelete). The row is not actually deleted, and embedded usages keep resolving, until `block_templates_publish` runs. Refuses to stage a delete if any posts still embed it as a global template — remove or convert those usages first.

tools.name: block_templates_fork
tools.desc: Duplicate a published block template into a new draft template tied to the original via parent_template_id. Use when you need to riff on a template without touching the original (e.g. building a variant of a hero block for a specific landing page). Returns the new template id + an approval URL.

args.name: id
args.desc: Source template id to fork.

args.name: slugSuffix
args.desc: Optional suffix appended before the unique fork tag in the new slug.

tools.name: block_templates_get
tools.desc: Fetch full template including its blocks JSON.

tools.name: block_templates_list
tools.desc: List reusable CMS block templates. Global templates are shared across clients.

tools.name: block_templates_publish
tools.desc: Promote a single block template draft to live. If draft.pendingDelete: the row is removed. If draft.pendingCreate: the draft flag is cleared (template becomes visible in the picker). Otherwise: draft fields are applied onto the live columns (bumping `version` when `blocks` changed) and draft is cleared. Subject to the same approval gate as other CMS writes.

tools.name: block_templates_update
tools.desc: Stage changes to a block template into its draft jsonb overlay. The live columns and version are untouched — the picker and global-sync paths keep using the published copy until `block_templates_publish` is called.

tools.name: booking_analytics_get
tools.desc: Return booking performance aggregates for the client over a time window: total paid bookings, revenue (base + add-on), cancelled count, total guests, and average booking value. All figures are client-scoped.

args.name: days
args.desc: Look-back window in days (default 30, max 365).

tools.name: booking_pages_create
tools.desc: Create a new bookable service / appointment type. Defaults: 30-min duration, free, Mon–Fri 09–17 America/New_York, individual booking, fixed assignment. The page starts `active=false`; approve the returned URL (or pass `active:true` explicitly) to flip it live. Returns the slim row + approval envelope.

args.name: price
args.desc: Price in cents. 0 = free.

args.name: priceLabel
args.desc: Free-text price display (e.g. "Starts at $200").

args.name: duration
args.desc: Minutes. Default 30.

args.name: availability
args.desc: Day-of-week + time-range schedule. Defaults to Mon–Fri 09–17 in `timezone`.

args.name: assignedMembers
args.desc: User ids on the rotation.

args.name: questions
args.desc: BookingQuestion[] — { id, label, type: text|textarea|select, required, options? }

args.name: styling
args.desc: BookingPageStyling — { primaryColor?, backgroundColor?, textColor?, headingFont?, bodyFont?, borderRadius?, buttonPrimary*?, hideTitle?, hideLogo? }

args.name: active
args.desc: Whether the booking page is immediately public. Default false; approving the returned link flips it true.

tools.name: booking_pages_get
tools.desc: Full booking page config including availability, questions, and feature toggles.

tools.name: booking_pages_list
tools.desc: List bookable services / appointment types (booking pages) for the client.

tools.name: booking_pages_update
tools.desc: Patch any combination of fields on a booking page. Same field set as booking_pages_create. Mints a fresh approval URL on every call — the old URL stays valid in whatever state it was already in. To delete a booking page, set `active=false` and flag it for cleanup; there is no destructive delete tool today.

tools.name: bookings_cancel
tools.desc: Cancel a booking. Marks status=cancelled and stamps cancelledAt. This does NOT auto-refund payment or remove Google Calendar events — handle those in the UI or via separate tools when they exist.

args.name: reason
args.desc: Internal note appended to booking.notes.

tools.name: bookings_get
tools.desc: Fetch a single booking by id.

tools.name: bookings_list
tools.desc: List scheduled bookings for the client. Filter by booking page, status, or date range. Use this to answer "what's on my calendar this week".

args.name: startAfter
args.desc: ISO datetime — only bookings with startTime >= this.

args.name: endBefore
args.desc: ISO datetime — only bookings with startTime <= this.

tools.name: bookings_update
tools.desc: Edit booking fields (times, status, notes, assignee, check-in). Time changes DO NOT automatically push to Google Calendar or notify the guest.

args.name: startTime
args.desc: ISO datetime.

args.name: endTime
args.desc: ISO datetime.

tools.name: brain_apply_classifications
tools.desc: Persist classifier output from brain_classify_notes: writes the brain_notes.status enum and attaches the matching reserved taxonomy topics. Rows below `minConfidence` (default 0.7) are routed to the AI review queue when `routeBelowMinToReview` is true (default), otherwise silently skipped. Idempotent — re-applying counts existing attachments as `attachmentsExisted`. Echo: { notesUpdated, topicsAttached, attachmentsExisted, routedToReview, skippedTotal, skipped (first 20) }.

tools.name: brain_approve_review_item
tools.desc: Approve a pending AI proposal. For "task" proposals this materializes a brain_tasks row. Optionally edit the payload before approving. AUDITED.

tools.name: brain_bulk_update_notes
tools.desc: Apply one of: soft_delete, restore, hard_delete, add_tags, remove_tags, replace_tag_prefix to up to 500 notes. Returns { updated, skipped }. Cross-tenant ids are silently skipped.

tools.name: brain_classify_notes
tools.desc: Run the LLM classifier across knowledge notes to assign source / slate-area / audience / content-type / recency / competitor / status facets. Pass an explicit `noteIds` array OR `all:true` (one is required). `dryRun:true` (DEFAULT) returns counts + a 5-row sample only — token-budget safe for thousands of notes. `dryRun:false` returns the full per-note classifications (minus `reasoning`) so they can be fed to brain_apply_classifications. No DB writes either way — this tool only previews.

args.name: dryRun
args.desc: When true (default), return counts + 5-row sample only. When false, return all classifications (without reasoning).

tools.name: brain_create_meeting
tools.desc: Create a meeting from pasted transcript text. Optionally link to a CRM company or deal at creation time. Use this when the user gives you raw meeting notes — never call this with content the user did not provide.

tools.name: brain_create_note
tools.desc: Save a knowledge note. The primary write surface for AI-driven web ingestion: pass `sourceUrl` to record provenance and source="crawl" when ingesting from the web. Body is markdown, capped at 50KB. Pre-check for an existing note via brain_list_notes(sourceUrl=...) before creating to avoid duplicates.

args.name: sourceUrl
args.desc: Original URL the content came from (for crawled notes).

tools.name: brain_create_note_from_template
tools.desc: Apply a template (resolving {{today}}, {{userName}}, etc.) and create a new note. Mirrors POST /portal/brain/knowledge/from-template/[id]. Slim echo (no body) — fetch full content via brain_get_note.

tools.name: brain_create_note_template
tools.desc: Define a reusable note template. Body is markdown — supports {{variables}} resolved by lib/brain/template.ts. Returns 409-equivalent error if a template with this name already exists for the client.

tools.name: brain_create_relationship
tools.desc: Start tracking a CRM company or deal as a Brain relationship. Idempotent — returns the existing overlay if one exists for the same target.

tools.name: brain_create_saved_search
tools.desc: Pin a knowledge filter set to the sidebar. scope="shared" makes it team-visible (userId IS NULL); scope="personal" (default) scopes to the caller. Returns identity echo only — re-fetch via brain_get_saved_search if you need the filters back.

tools.name: brain_create_task
tools.desc: Create a Brain task directly. Use brain_propose_task instead when the user is reviewing your suggestions.

tools.name: brain_dashboard_summary
tools.desc: Return the command-center snapshot: needs-review meetings, overdue/blocked/upcoming tasks, stale prospects, priority relationships, recent meetings, and high-level counts (including decisionsCount + topicsCount from the brain-restructure entities).

tools.name: brain_decisions_create
tools.desc: Create a new accepted decision. Heavy text fields (decision, rationale, context, alternativesConsidered) live in the input; the echo is slim ({ id, status, decidedAt }) so the caller does not round-trip the prose it just authored. AUDITED.

args.name: decidedAt
args.desc: ISO timestamp; defaults to now.

tools.name: brain_decisions_get
tools.desc: Fetch a decision by id with its supersedes chain (ancestors + descendants). Heavy text fields (context, rationale, decision, alternatives) are opt-in via `include` to stay token-light; chain summary rows are always slim ({ id, title, decidedAt, status }).

tools.name: brain_decisions_list
tools.desc: List decisions with optional filters (status, reversibility, decision-maker, date range, supersededOnly, topicId). Slim by default — heavy text fields (context, rationale, decision text, alternatives) are opt-in via `include`. Paginated via { items, total, limit, offset }; limit capped at 100.

args.name: dateFrom
args.desc: ISO date — decidedAt >= this.

args.name: dateTo
args.desc: ISO date — decidedAt <= this.

args.name: topicId
args.desc: Currently a no-op pass-through; helper has a TODO to JOIN brain_entity_topics. Accepted without erroring so callers can future-proof.

tools.name: brain_decisions_reject
tools.desc: Soft-delete by transitioning status → "rejected". Decisions are immutable history — no row is ever DELETEd. Idempotent. AUDITED.

tools.name: brain_decisions_supersede
tools.desc: Atomically create a successor decision and link it back to the old one (old.status → "superseded", old.supersededByDecisionId → new.id). Use this whenever you need to change rationale, decision text, or reversibility. Echo: { previous, current }. AUDITED.

tools.name: brain_decisions_update
tools.desc: Patch mutable fields (title, context, decisionMakerId, anchors, confidentialityLevel, alternativesConsidered) on an existing decision. Attempts to mutate `decision`, `rationale`, or `reversibility` are REJECTED — those changes require `brain_decisions_supersede` (immutable history). Echo is { id, updatedFields }. AUDITED.

tools.name: brain_delete_note
tools.desc: Two-stage delete matching the portal. Default (force=false) soft-deletes — note moves to trash and can be restored via brain_restore_note; if the note was already trashed, this hard-deletes it. Pass force=true to hard-delete on the first call. Hard delete cleans up any attached S3 object. AUDITED.

args.name: force
args.desc: When true, skip the soft-delete stage and hard-delete immediately.

tools.name: brain_delete_note_template
tools.desc: Permanently delete a template. Existing notes created from it are unaffected.

tools.name: brain_delete_saved_search
tools.desc: Remove a saved-search pin from the sidebar.

tools.name: brain_document_acknowledgments_list_for_document
tools.desc: Audit trail — every (version, person, acknowledgedAt) recorded against this document. Optional filters by versionId or personId. Returns slim rows { ackId, versionId, versionNumber, personId, personName, acknowledgedAt, acknowledgmentNote }. Cap limit 100.

tools.name: brain_document_acknowledgments_list_for_person
tools.desc: Every document this person has acknowledged, newest first. Returns { ackId, documentId, documentTitle, versionNumber, acknowledgedAt } per row. Cap limit 100.

tools.name: brain_document_compliance_report
tools.desc: The canonical "who has read this, who hasn't" view. Expands org-unit required-reads to active member person ids, partitions the assigned-person universe into acknowledged / pending / overdue against the document's currentPublishedVersionId, and returns full id arrays + a summary count rollup. A document with no current published version yields acknowledged=0 (nothing to ack against yet).

tools.name: brain_document_required_reads_assign
tools.desc: Make a person OR an org_unit required to read this document. Idempotent on (documentId, targetType, targetId) — re-assigning updates pinnedVersionId + dueAt. When targetType="org_unit" and expandOrgUnit=true, fans out to one row per ACTIVE member of the unit (current snapshot — new members later still need a re-assign). Echo: { assigned, alreadyAssigned, expandedTo? }.

tools.name: brain_document_required_reads_list_for_document
tools.desc: Who is REQUIRED to read this document? Returns rows { id, targetType, targetId, targetName (resolved from brain_people.fullName or brain_org_units.name), pinnedVersionId, dueAt, assignedAt }. Filter by targetType to view only person- or only org_unit-scoped assignments. Cap limit 100.

tools.name: brain_document_required_reads_list_for_person
tools.desc: What does THIS person have to read? Returns the person's direct required-read assignments with each row's acknowledged status, the version they actually need to ack (pinned or the doc's currentPublishedVersionId), and an `ackId`/`acknowledgedAt` when present. `status` filters: `open` = unacknowledged, `acknowledged` = already done, `all` = both (default). Org-unit-scoped assignments NOT expanded — use brain_document_compliance_report for that view.

tools.name: brain_document_required_reads_remove
tools.desc: Delete a required-read row. Default refuses if any acknowledgments reference it (history-preservation) — returns structured { error: "has_acks" }. Pass force=true to unlink (the FK is set-null, so the acks survive but lose their requiredReadId pointer). Echo on success: { removed: true }.

tools.name: brain_document_versions_edit_draft
tools.desc: Patch the document's draft body / summary / changeNotes. If no draft exists (last action was a publish), creates a new draft seeded from the latest version's body — so editors don't lose context. Refuses if the document is archived. Echo: { documentId, versionId, versionNumber, isDraft: true }.

tools.name: brain_document_versions_get
tools.desc: Fetch one specific version of a document — the caller asked for THIS version, so the full markdown `body` ships by default. Pass `include: ["changeNotes"]` or `["summary"]` to attach those extra fields too.

tools.name: brain_document_versions_list
tools.desc: List a document's versions (newest first). Slim by default — returns { id, versionNumber, isDraft, publishedAt, title }. Pass `include: ["body"]` to attach the full markdown body per row (heavy); `["changeNotes"]` to attach the per-version change log; `["summary"]` to attach the optional executive summary. Cap limit 100.

tools.name: brain_documents_acknowledge
tools.desc: Record a (documentId, versionId, personId) acknowledgment. Idempotent — re-acking the same tuple returns the existing row without a duplicate audit entry. If requiredReadId is omitted, auto-links to a matching person-target required-read for this (documentId, personId) when one exists. Echo: { ackId, documentId, versionId, personId, acknowledgedAt }.

tools.name: brain_documents_archive
tools.desc: Soft cancellation — sets status="archived", archivedAt=now(), archiveReason=reason. Document remains in the database (cascade-deletion happens only on brain_documents_delete). Echo: { id, status: "archived", archivedAt }.

tools.name: brain_documents_create
tools.desc: Create a new document seeded with an empty v1 draft. Slug is auto-derived from title (collisions per tenant suffix -2, -3, …). Echoes { id, slug, status, version1Id } — call brain_documents_get for the full row. To populate the body, follow up with brain_document_versions_edit_draft, then brain_documents_publish.

tools.name: brain_documents_delete
tools.desc: Hard delete the document and (via FK cascade) every version, required-read, link, and acknowledgment. Refuses by default if any acknowledgments exist — history preservation matters more than tidiness. Pass force=true to cascade. Returns structured { error: "document_has_acks", ackCount } on conflict. Echo on success: { id, deleted: true }.

tools.name: brain_documents_get
tools.desc: Fetch a single document + its slim version list + resolved links. Heavy fields are opt-in: pass `includeBody=true` to attach `currentPublishedVersion` and `currentDraftVersion` full rows (each carries the markdown body); pass `includeAllVersions=true` to attach every version's full row in `versions` (can be very large). Without either, you get { document, versions (slim: id/versionNumber/isDraft/publishedAt/title), links }.

tools.name: brain_documents_link
tools.desc: Attach a polymorphic entity (topic, initiative, decision, meeting, glossary_term, person) to a document. Idempotent — re-posting the same (documentId, entityType, entityId) returns alreadyLinked=true with linkId=null. Echo: { linkId, alreadyLinked }.

tools.name: brain_documents_list
tools.desc: List versioned SOPs / policies / required-reads. Slim by default — returns { id, title, slug, category, status, ownerId, currentPublishedVersionId, publishedAt, versionCount, requiredReadCount, ackCount } per row. Pass `include: ["body"]` to hydrate each row with the current published version's body (heavy, opt in). Filters: status, category, ownerId, search. Cap limit 100.

tools.name: brain_documents_promote_from_note
tools.desc: Create a new document seeded from an existing brain_note — the note's body becomes the v1 draft's body. Title defaults to the note's title (or first non-empty line of the body). The document's sourceNoteId points back to the original. Echo: { documentId, slug, version1Id }.

tools.name: brain_documents_publish
tools.desc: Flip the current draft to a published version, atomically updating the document's currentPublishedVersionId + status="published" + publishedAt (first-publish only). Refuses if no draft exists OR if the draft body is empty — call brain_document_versions_edit_draft first. On empty body, returns structured { error: "empty_draft_body" }. Echo: { id, versionId, versionNumber, status: "published", publishedAt }.

tools.name: brain_documents_unarchive
tools.desc: Reverse archive: clears archivedAt + archiveReason and restores status to "published" (if a published version exists) or "draft" otherwise. Echo: { id, status }.

tools.name: brain_documents_unlink
tools.desc: Remove a polymorphic (documentId, entityType, entityId) link. Echo: { removed: boolean } — false if no matching link existed.

tools.name: brain_documents_update
tools.desc: Patch document-level metadata (title, category, ownerId, confidentialityLevel, defaultTopicIds). Status changes are REJECTED here — use brain_documents_publish / brain_documents_archive / brain_documents_unarchive. Returns a structured { error: "use_publish_or_archive" } if the patch attempts a status change. Echoes { id, updatedFields }.

tools.name: brain_expertise_tags_create
tools.desc: Create a per-tenant expertise tag. Slug is auto-derived from name; collisions get a `-2`, `-3` suffix. Echoes `{ id, slug }`.

tools.name: brain_expertise_tags_delete
tools.desc: Delete an expertise tag. Default refuses if any person still holds it — pass `force: true` to cascade-detach. Returns a structured `{ error: "in_use", peopleAttached }` shape on conflict.

tools.name: brain_expertise_tags_list
tools.desc: List per-tenant expertise tags. Slim row by default — pass `include: ["description"]` to inline the description text. `peopleCount` is always populated. Filter by `search` (ILIKE on name + description) or `source` ("manual" | "ai_suggested").

tools.name: brain_expertise_tags_merge
tools.desc: Re-attach every brain_person_expertise row from `sourceTagId` to `targetTagId`, then delete the source tag. Levels on target are preserved; if target has no level but source had one, source's level is copied. Echoes `{ peopleReattached, sourceDeleted: true }`.

tools.name: brain_expertise_tags_update
tools.desc: Patch name or description on an expertise tag. Slug stays stable (renames do not change the URL). Echoes `{ id, updatedFields }`.

tools.name: brain_get_company
tools.desc: Get a CRM company with its linked contacts and open deals.

tools.name: brain_get_contact
tools.desc: Get a CRM contact with their linked company and any open deals they own.

tools.name: brain_get_deal
tools.desc: Get a CRM deal with its linked company, primary contact, and stage info.

tools.name: brain_get_meeting
tools.desc: Get a meeting with participants, transcript, AI summary, and the linked CRM record (if any).

tools.name: brain_get_note
tools.desc: Fetch a single note with its full body. Use brain_list_notes to find IDs.

tools.name: brain_get_note_template
tools.desc: Fetch a template by id, including the full markdown body.

tools.name: brain_get_post
tools.desc: Get a post including its full block JSON (posts.content). Validates tenancy via the website ownership.

tools.name: brain_get_relationship
tools.desc: Get a relationship overlay by id with linked CRM record, contacts, recent meetings, and open tasks.

tools.name: brain_get_review_item
tools.desc: Get a single pending or resolved AI proposal by id, including the full proposed payload.

tools.name: brain_get_saved_search
tools.desc: Fetch a saved search by id, including the full filters JSON.

tools.name: brain_get_task
tools.desc: Fetch a single Brain task by id.

tools.name: brain_glossary_bulk_import
tools.desc: Insert or update up to 200 terms in one call. Upsert is per-tenant on slug (auto-derived from `term`) — existing rows have their definition/shortDefinition/aliases/category replaced; new rows are inserted with status="active" and source="manual". A single audit row is written after the batch. Echoes { created, updated, errors }.

tools.name: brain_glossary_create
tools.desc: Add a new term. Slug is auto-derived from `term` (lowercase, dash-separated); collisions per tenant suffix `-2`, `-3`, …. Default status="active", source="manual", aliases=[], relatedTermIds=[]. Echoes { id, slug } only — call brain_glossary_get for the full row.

tools.name: brain_glossary_delete
tools.desc: Hard delete. Also prunes this id from every OTHER term's relatedTermIds list. Audit row written before the delete. Echoes { id, deleted, prunedRelatedTermFromCount }.

tools.name: brain_glossary_get
tools.desc: Fetch a single term + its "see also" related terms (joined from the relatedTermIds JSON array, cross-tenant ids filtered out). Slim by default — omits full `definition` and `aliases` from the main term unless `include` is passed. Related terms are always slim (id/term/slug/shortDefinition).

tools.name: brain_glossary_list
tools.desc: List tenant glossary terms (acronyms, codenames, jargon). Slim by default: returns id, term, slug, shortDefinition, status, category, ownerId, aliasCount. To receive full `definition` and full `aliases`, pass include=["definition"] / ["aliases"]. Filters: status, category, search, ownerId. Cap limit 100.

args.name: search
args.desc: Substring match on term, aliases, and definition.

tools.name: brain_glossary_lookup
tools.desc: The marquee tool: substring + alias-array match against ACTIVE glossary terms with a scored ranking (exact term 10 / exact alias 8 / term prefix 5 / alias prefix 4 / term substring 3 / alias substring 2 / definition substring 1). Use BEFORE answering any factual question that may contain tenant-specific acronyms or codenames so the workspace's preferred definition is used. Cap limit 25, default 10.

tools.name: brain_glossary_update
tools.desc: Patch any field on a glossary term EXCEPT slug (which is stable for external URLs). Echoes { id, updatedFields }.

tools.name: brain_goals_checkin
tools.desc: Drop a progress check-in — updates currentMetric / lastProgressNote / lastCheckedInAt. When status is omitted but currentMetric is provided, the auto-classifier picks the new status. Not audit-logged (lastCheckedInAt is the breadcrumb). Echo: { id, status, currentMetric, lastCheckedInAt }.

tools.name: brain_goals_create
tools.desc: Create a goal under an existing initiative (must be in the same tenant). Echo: { id, status, initiativeId } — re-fetch via brain_goals_get for the full row.

tools.name: brain_goals_delete
tools.desc: Hard-delete a goal (leaf row — no cascade impact). Echo: { id, deleted: true }.

tools.name: brain_goals_get
tools.desc: Get one goal by id with a slim parent-initiative reference ({ id, name, slug, status }). Heavy text fields (description, lastProgressNote) are opt-in via `include`.

tools.name: brain_goals_list
tools.desc: List goals for this tenant. Slim by default — returns { id, initiativeId, title, status, ownerId, targetDate, sortOrder, currentMetric, targetMetric, unit } per row. Pass `include: ["description"]` or `["lastProgressNote"]` to opt into heavier text fields.

tools.name: brain_goals_update
tools.desc: Patch fields on a goal. Status changes are allowed here (unlike initiatives). Echo: { id, updatedFields }.

tools.name: brain_initiatives_close
tools.desc: Terminal status transition — outcome must be "completed" or "cancelled". Requires at least one of `reason` / `lessonsLearned`. If lessonsLearned is provided, a brain_note is auto-created with the text and pinned-linked back. Echo: { id, status, closedAt, noteId? }.

tools.name: brain_initiatives_create
tools.desc: Create a multi-quarter initiative. Echo: { id, slug, status } — re-fetch via brain_initiatives_get for the full row.

tools.name: brain_initiatives_get
tools.desc: Get one initiative by id. Pass `includeGoals=true` to inline ordered goals, `includeLinks=true` to inline resolved linked-entity rows (also returns byType counts when present). Heavy text fields (description, lessonsLearned) are opt-in via `include`.

tools.name: brain_initiatives_link
tools.desc: Attach a polymorphic entity (task, note, meeting, decision, topic, crm_deal, crm_company, person, org_unit, glossary_term) to an initiative. Idempotent — re-posting the same (initiativeId, entityType, entityId) returns alreadyLinked=true with linkId=null. Echo: { linkId, alreadyLinked }.

tools.name: brain_initiatives_links
tools.desc: List the polymorphic entities (tasks, notes, meetings, decisions, topics, CRM deals, CRM companies) linked to an initiative. Returns resolved display rows + { total, byType counts }.

tools.name: brain_initiatives_list
tools.desc: List initiatives for this tenant. Slim by default — returns { id, name, slug, status, priority, ownerId, targetDate, goalCount } per row. Pass `include: ["description"]` or `["lessonsLearned"]` to opt into heavier text fields. Filters: status, ownerId, priority, hasOpenGoals, targetDateBefore (ISO).

args.name: targetDateBefore
args.desc: ISO date — return only initiatives whose targetDate is before this.

tools.name: brain_initiatives_reopen
tools.desc: Reopen a previously closed initiative — only allowed from `completed` or `cancelled`. Sets status="active" and clears closedAt. Echo: { id, status }. Returns a structured error { error: "non_terminal_status" } if the current status is not terminal.

tools.name: brain_initiatives_unlink
tools.desc: Remove a polymorphic link from an initiative. Echo: { removed: boolean } — false if no matching link existed.

tools.name: brain_initiatives_update
tools.desc: Patch fields on an initiative. Status changes are NOT allowed here — use brain_initiatives_close or brain_initiatives_reopen. Echo: { id, updatedFields }. Returns a structured error { error: "use_close_or_reopen" } if a status change is attempted.

tools.name: brain_link_meeting
tools.desc: Set or clear a meeting's CRM link (company or deal). Pass companyId=null or dealId=null to clear.

tools.name: brain_list_companies
tools.desc: List CRM companies for this tenant. Optional fuzzy search on name + domain. Use brain_search for semantic matching across all entity types; this is for browsing/filtering by structured fields.

args.name: search
args.desc: ILIKE on name and domain.

tools.name: brain_list_contacts
tools.desc: List CRM contacts. Optional filter by companyId or fuzzy search on name + email.

args.name: search
args.desc: ILIKE on first_name, last_name, email.

tools.name: brain_list_deals
tools.desc: List CRM deals. Optional filter by status (open/won/lost), priority, or stageId.

tools.name: brain_list_meetings
tools.desc: List meetings. Optional filter by status (draft/processing/needs_review/approved).

tools.name: brain_list_note_history
tools.desc: Audit log for one note: created, updated, soft_deleted, restored, hard_deleted, attachment_cleared, etc. Slim by default (omits metadata.diff and other large blobs). Pass includeDiff=true to receive the full metadata payload.

args.name: includeDiff
args.desc: When true, include the full metadata blob (may contain diffs). Default false.

tools.name: brain_list_note_templates
tools.desc: List reusable note templates (markdown bodies with {{variables}}). Slim by default (omits the body text); pass includeBody=true to inline bodies — they can be multi-KB each.

tools.name: brain_list_notes
tools.desc: List/search notes in Company Brain Knowledge. Use this BEFORE crawling a URL to dedupe — pass `sourceUrl` for an exact match or `sourceUrlStartsWith` for a domain-wide check. Slim by default (no body — call brain_get_note for the full row); paginated via { items, total, limit, offset }.

args.name: search
args.desc: ILIKE on title and body.

args.name: tag
args.desc: Match a single tag.

args.name: sourceUrl
args.desc: Exact source URL match — for dedup.

args.name: sourceUrlStartsWith
args.desc: Prefix match on source URL — e.g. "https://docs.example.com/" to find everything ingested from that site.

args.name: trashed
args.desc: When true, return only soft-deleted notes (the trash bin). Default false.

tools.name: brain_list_posts
tools.desc: List posts owned by this tenant via client_websites. Optional filter by websiteId, published flag, or post_type. Bodies are returned as serialized block JSON — call brain_get_post for the full record.

tools.name: brain_list_relationships
tools.desc: List relationship overlays. Filter by type, owner, priority, status, or staleness.

tools.name: brain_list_review_items
tools.desc: List items in the AI proposal queue. Default: pending only. Filter by source meeting via sourceId.

tools.name: brain_list_saved_searches
tools.desc: List the caller's sidebar-pinned filter sets. scope=mine returns personal pins only, scope=shared returns team pins (userId IS NULL), scope=all (default) returns both. Slim by default (no filters JSON); pass includeFilters=true to receive the filter payloads inline.

tools.name: brain_list_tasks
tools.desc: List Brain tasks. Filter by status, owner, meeting, needs-review flag.

tools.name: brain_org_units_add_member
tools.desc: Attach a person to an org unit. Idempotent — re-attaching updates `primary` and `roleInUnit`. Marking primary flips primary=false on the person's other memberships. Echoes `{ alreadyMember, primary }`.

tools.name: brain_org_units_create
tools.desc: Create a hierarchical org unit. Slug auto-derived; path computed from parent. Echoes `{ id, slug, path }`.

tools.name: brain_org_units_delete
tools.desc: Delete an org unit. Default refuses if it has members or children — pass `force: true` to detach members and re-parent children up one level. Returns structured `{ error: "in_use", memberCount, childCount }` on conflict.

tools.name: brain_org_units_get
tools.desc: Fetch an org unit with its ancestor chain and members (personId / fullName / title / primary / roleInUnit).

tools.name: brain_org_units_list
tools.desc: Flat list of org units for this tenant, ordered by path. Slim row by default (no description) — pass `include: ["descriptions"]` to inline the description text. `memberCount` is always populated.

tools.name: brain_org_units_merge
tools.desc: Re-parent `sourceId`'s children under `targetId`, re-attach `sourceId`'s members to `targetId` (dedup-safe), then delete `sourceId`. Echoes `{ sourceId, targetId, membersReattached, childrenReparented }`.

tools.name: brain_org_units_move
tools.desc: Move an org unit under a new parent (or to root with `newParentId: null`). Rewrites the path prefix for the moved unit AND every descendant. Cycle-guarded. Echoes `{ id, path, descendantsRepathed }`.

tools.name: brain_org_units_remove_member
tools.desc: Detach a person from an org unit. `removed: false` means the membership row did not exist.

tools.name: brain_org_units_set_primary
tools.desc: Mark `orgUnitId` as the primary membership for `personId`. Flips primary=false on the person's other memberships in the same transaction. Requires the membership to already exist — call brain_org_units_add_member first if not.

tools.name: brain_org_units_tree
tools.desc: Nested tree of org units for this tenant. Each node carries `childCount` and `memberCount`. Slim by default (no description) — pass `include: ["descriptions"]` to inline.

tools.name: brain_org_units_update
tools.desc: Patch fields on an org unit. Slug + path stay stable on rename. Echoes `{ id, updatedFields }`. Use brain_org_units_move to re-parent.

tools.name: brain_people_attach_expertise
tools.desc: Attach an expertise tag with an optional 1–4 proficiency level. Idempotent — `alreadyAttached: true` means the row already existed (level may have been updated).

tools.name: brain_people_create
tools.desc: Add an internal person (employee / advisor / contractor). Echoes only `{ id, status }` — re-fetch via brain_people_get for the full record.

tools.name: brain_people_delete
tools.desc: Delete a person. Cascades org-unit memberships and expertise junctions; reports-to chains pointing at this person are nulled out.

tools.name: brain_people_detach_expertise
tools.desc: Remove an expertise tag from a person. `detached: false` means the row did not exist.

tools.name: brain_people_get
tools.desc: Fetch a person with manager, direct reports, org-unit memberships, and expertise tags. Slim person fields by default — pass `include: ["notes", "profileUrls"]` to opt into heavy fields.

tools.name: brain_people_list
tools.desc: List internal people (employees / advisors / contractors). Slim row by default — pass `include: ["notes", "profileUrls"]` to opt into heavy fields. Filter by status / orgUnitId / expertiseTagId / managerId / search.

tools.name: brain_people_update
tools.desc: Patch fields on a person. Manager change is cycle-guarded — assigning a descendant as the manager returns `{ error: "manager_cycle" }`. Echoes only `{ id, updatedFields }`.

tools.name: brain_playbook_run_steps_complete
tools.desc: Explicitly mark a run-step completed (used for task/decision/review_item kinds that don't auto-complete). Optionally record the entity this step produced. After the mutation, advanceRun chains forward. Echo: { stepId, status: "completed" }.

tools.name: brain_playbook_run_steps_skip
tools.desc: Mark a run-step skipped (the step is treated as terminal for routing but with no result). Optional `reason` is stored on the row. After the mutation, advanceRun chains forward. Echo: { stepId, status: "skipped" }.

tools.name: brain_playbook_runs_abort
tools.desc: Stop a run mid-flight. Any still-active step rows are marked skipped with the abort reason. Echo: { runId, status: "aborted" }.

tools.name: brain_playbook_runs_active_for_entity
tools.desc: Returns active + paused runs anchored to the given entity via brain_playbook_links — e.g. "what onboarding playbook is in flight for this person?". Slim row shape, same as brain_playbook_runs_list.

tools.name: brain_playbook_runs_advance
tools.desc: Resolve any active `branch` run-steps and chain forward to next steps. Task/decision/review_item/wait steps stay active until explicit completion — this tool does not touch them. Echo: { runId, newActiveStepKeys, newStatus }.

tools.name: brain_playbook_runs_get
tools.desc: Get one run by id with { run, playbook (slim: id/name/slug/status), steps (per-run state), links }. Heavy JSON columns (`context`, `triggerPayload`) are opt-in via `include`.

tools.name: brain_playbook_runs_list
tools.desc: List runs for this tenant. Slim row default — { id, playbookId, playbookName, label, status, startedAt, completedAt, stepProgress: { completed, total } }. Filter by status and / or playbookId. Cap limit at 100.

tools.name: brain_playbook_runs_start
tools.desc: Spawn a new run of an active playbook. `context` is the variable bag step configs template against (e.g. { person: { fullName: "Jane" } }). `links` anchors the run to polymorphic entities (initiative, person, crm_company, crm_deal, meeting, decision). Entry steps fire immediately within the start tx. Echo: { runId, status: "active", firstStepKeys: string[] }.

tools.name: brain_playbooks_activate
tools.desc: Flip status from `draft` to `active`. Refuses if the playbook has zero steps OR the step graph fails DAG validation (cycles, missing next-step refs, no entry point). On DAG failure returns a structured error { error: "dag_invalid", errors: string[] }. Echo on success: { id, status: "active" }.

tools.name: brain_playbooks_add_step
tools.desc: Append a step to a playbook. The step `key` is a stable identifier within the playbook (used by nextStepKeys + run state). `sortOrder` auto-picks (append) when omitted. Echo: { id, key } — re-fetch via brain_playbooks_get for the full row.

tools.name: brain_playbooks_archive
tools.desc: Flip status to `archived`. Refuses while pending/active/paused runs exist unless `force=true`. Echo on success: { id, status: "archived" }. Returns a structured error { error: "active_runs_exist", message } if force is omitted and active runs block the transition.

tools.name: brain_playbooks_create
tools.desc: Create a new playbook (always starts in `draft`). Use brain_playbooks_add_step to attach steps, then brain_playbooks_activate once the DAG is valid. Echo: { id, slug, status }.

tools.name: brain_playbooks_delete
tools.desc: Hard delete. Refuses while any runs exist (active or historical) unless `force=true` — force cascades through runs/run-steps/links. Echo on success: { id, deleted: true }. Returns a structured error { error: "runs_exist", message } if force is omitted and runs block the delete.

tools.name: brain_playbooks_get
tools.desc: Get one playbook by id with its ordered steps. Slim by default — step rows return { id, key, name, kind, nextStepKeys, sortOrder } and the playbook omits description. Pass `include: ["description"]` to inline the playbook description, `["stepConfigs"]` to inline each step's config + condition + description blobs.

tools.name: brain_playbooks_list
tools.desc: List multi-step playbooks for this tenant. Slim by default — returns { id, name, slug, status, category, triggerKind, ownerId, stepCount, activeRunCount } per row. Pass `include: ["description"]`, `["triggerConfig"]`, or `["defaultTopicIds"]` to opt into heavier fields. Filters: status, category, triggerKind, ownerId.

tools.name: brain_playbooks_remove_step
tools.desc: Remove a step from a playbook. Defensive — refuses if any run-step row references it (delete the affected runs first). Also walks sibling steps and strips this step's key from their nextStepKeys arrays so the DAG stays clean. Echo: { stepId, deleted: true }.

tools.name: brain_playbooks_reorder_steps
tools.desc: Atomically re-sortOrder the given step ids. All ids must belong to the same playbook + tenant; otherwise the whole batch is rejected. Steps not in `orderedStepIds` are left untouched. Echo: { playbookId, count }.

tools.name: brain_playbooks_update
tools.desc: Patch fields on a playbook definition. Status changes are NOT allowed here — use brain_playbooks_activate or brain_playbooks_archive. Echo: { id, updatedFields }. Returns a structured error { error: "use_activate_or_archive" } if a status change is attempted.

tools.name: brain_playbooks_update_step
tools.desc: Patch fields on an existing step. Echo: { id, updatedFields }.

tools.name: brain_propose_task
tools.desc: Stage a suggested task as a pending AI review item — visible in /portal/brain/communications/[id]/review for the user to approve, edit, or reject. Prefer this over brain_create_task when you're unsure or when the suggestion came from analysis the user hasn't directly authorized.

tools.name: brain_reject_review_item
tools.desc: Reject a pending AI proposal. AUDITED.

tools.name: brain_restore_note
tools.desc: Move a trashed note back to the active list. No-op (returns the note) if it was not deleted. Mirrors POST /portal/brain/knowledge/[id]/restore.

tools.name: brain_review_items_list_for_reviewer
tools.desc: List review items where suggested_reviewer_person_id matches the given brain_people.id. Useful for "show me items routed to me" queries. Capped at 50 rows; filter by status (default pending).

tools.name: brain_review_items_suggest_reviewer
tools.desc: Score active brain_people for who should review this AI proposal — based on topic-expertise match, org-unit context, past approval history for this proposed_type, and current workload. Persists the top candidate (when score >= 3) on suggested_reviewer_person_id/score/reason. Returns the suggestion or null. AUDITED.

tools.name: brain_search
tools.desc: Hybrid lexical + semantic search across the entire workspace: knowledge notes, meetings, CRM companies and contacts, deals, tasks, relationships, and pages. Returns ranked hits with snippets and citation URLs. Use this before answering any factual question about the workspace — never guess.

tools.name: brain_topics_attach
tools.desc: Bulk-attach one or more topics to a single (entityType, entityId) target. Idempotent — rows that already exist are reported as `alreadyAttached`. Cross-tenant topic ids are silently dropped. Echo: { attached, alreadyAttached }.

tools.name: brain_topics_create
tools.desc: Create a topic. Slug + path auto-derive from name; slug collisions get a `-2`, `-3`, … suffix. Echo: { id, slug, path, parentId }. AUDITED.

tools.name: brain_topics_delete
tools.desc: Delete a topic. Refuses if the topic has children (resolve via merge or by deleting children first). Refuses if any entities are attached unless `force=true`, which also drops the join rows. AUDITED.

tools.name: brain_topics_detach
tools.desc: Bulk-detach one or more topics from a single (entityType, entityId) target. Tenant-scoped; missing rows are a no-op. Echo: { detached }.

tools.name: brain_topics_entities
tools.desc: List the notes / meetings / tasks / decisions / relationship-overlays attached to a topic. Returns slim `{ entityType, entityId, title }` rows, a total, and a per-type tally (`byType`). Paginated; limit capped at 100.

tools.name: brain_topics_get
tools.desc: Fetch a topic by id with its breadcrumb (root → immediate parent, NOT including the topic itself). `description` is opt-in.

tools.name: brain_topics_import_from_tags
tools.desc: Walk every `brain_notes.tags` string, split `a/b/c` into a hierarchical chain of topics, find-or-create each segment, and attach every note bearing that tag to the leaf topic. Optional `tagPrefix` scopes to one branch. `dryRun=true` returns the report without writing. Idempotent — re-running adds nothing if no new tags appeared. Returns the full per-topic report (intentionally NOT slimmed — this IS the result the caller wants).

tools.name: brain_topics_list
tools.desc: List every topic for this tenant in path order (children sort under their parents). Slim by default — no `description`. Pass `includeEntityCounts=true` to add per-row `entityCount` (one extra group-by query).

args.name: tagPrefix
args.desc: Filter to topics whose path starts with `/<tagPrefix>` — useful after an import-from-tags run.

tools.name: brain_topics_merge
tools.desc: Fold `sourceId` into `targetId`: reattach all entity links (skipping dupes), reparent source's children under target (with full path rewrite), then delete source. Refuses to merge a topic into one of its own descendants. Echo: { sourceId, targetId, entitiesReattached, childrenReparented }. AUDITED.

tools.name: brain_topics_move
tools.desc: Move a topic under a new parent (pass `newParentId: null` to promote to root). Recomputes the affected subtree's materialized `path` atomically. Echo: { id, path, descendantsRepathed }. AUDITED.

tools.name: brain_topics_tree
tools.desc: Return the topic taxonomy as a nested tree with per-node `childCount` + `entityCount`. Descriptions are omitted by default; pass `includeDescriptions=true` to inline them (potentially multi-KB per node).

tools.name: brain_topics_update
tools.desc: Patch a topic. Rename DOES NOT change slug (stable URLs); use brain_topics_move for reparenting. Echo: { id, updatedFields }. AUDITED.

tools.name: brain_update_note
tools.desc: Patch fields on an existing note. Pass `null` for nullable fields to clear them.

tools.name: brain_update_note_template
tools.desc: Patch any field on a template. Returns identity echo + updatedAt; re-fetch via brain_get_note_template if you need the full body back.

tools.name: brain_update_relationship
tools.desc: Edit a Brain relationship overlay (priorities, summary, next review date, etc.). AUDITED.

tools.name: brain_update_saved_search
tools.desc: Patch fields on a saved search. Pass scope to move between personal and shared. Returns identity echo + updatedAt; re-fetch via brain_get_saved_search if you need the new filters.

tools.name: brain_update_task
tools.desc: Patch task fields (title, description, status, priority, due date, owner, blocked reason).

tools.name: brain_upsert_note_by_url
tools.desc: Idempotent crawl primitive: if a note already exists for this `sourceUrl`, update its title/body/tags; otherwise create a new one. Returns `{ note, created: boolean }`. Prefer this over brain_create_note when ingesting web pages.

tools.name: brain_who_knows
tools.desc: Resolve a free-text query to expertise tags (substring match on tag name + description), then rank people by matched-tag count, level bonus, and primary-org-unit bonus. The marquee tool — use this when the user asks "who knows about X" or "who should I talk to about Y".

tools.name: branding_audit
tools.desc: Run the rule-based consistency audit. Returns WCAG contrast issues, missing-field warnings, and structural problems.

tools.name: branding_check_contrast
tools.desc: Compute WCAG contrast ratio between two CSS colors. Returns ratio plus AA/AAA pass/fail.

args.name: foreground
args.desc: Foreground color (hex, rgb, or rgba).

args.name: background
args.desc: Background color (hex, rgb, or rgba).

tools.name: branding_create_profile
tools.desc: Create a new brand profile with colors, fonts, and logos. Pass isDefault:true to make it the client's default (unsets others).

tools.name: branding_delete_profile
tools.desc: Permanently delete a branding profile. Sites that referenced it will fall back to the client default profile.

tools.name: branding_get_messaging
tools.desc: Fetch tagline, value proposition, elevator pitch, tone, voice samples, differentiators.

tools.name: branding_get_profile
tools.desc: Get a full branding profile (colors, fonts, logos, button style). Omit profileId for the default profile.

tools.name: branding_list_profiles
tools.desc: List branding profiles for the authenticated client.

tools.name: branding_update_messaging
tools.desc: Update the client's brand voice / copy context (tagline, elevator pitch, value prop, tone, target audience, differentiators). Creates the row if it doesn't exist. Pass profileId to scope messaging to a specific brand profile; omit for the client-level default.

tools.name: branding_update_profile
tools.desc: Update any combination of colors, fonts, logos, or the isDefault flag on an existing profile.

tools.name: chat_conversation_reply
tools.desc: Send an agent reply to a visitor chat conversation. Verifies ownership before inserting.

args.name: conversationId
args.desc: ID of the conversation to reply to.

args.name: body
args.desc: Message body text.

tools.name: chat_conversation_update
tools.desc: Update the status and/or assigned user of a conversation. Verifies ownership before updating.

args.name: id
args.desc: Conversation ID.

args.name: status
args.desc: New status.

args.name: assignedUserId
args.desc: User ID to assign, or null to unassign.

tools.name: chat_conversations_get
tools.desc: Fetch a single chat conversation and its messages. Verifies the conversation belongs to the authenticated client.

args.name: id
args.desc: Conversation ID.

tools.name: chat_conversations_list
tools.desc: List chat conversations for this client. Optionally filter by widgetId or status.

args.name: widgetId
args.desc: Filter to a specific widget.

args.name: status
args.desc: Filter by conversation status.

args.name: limit
args.desc: Max results (default 25, max 100).

tools.name: chat_widgets_list
tools.desc: List all chat widgets configured for this client.

tools.name: client_get
tools.desc: Return the full client row (company, phone, website, address, email prefix, notes).

tools.name: client_update
tools.desc: Update the authenticated client's profile (company name, phone, public website URL, address, notes). Cannot change email or stripe customer id via MCP.

tools.name: contracts_create
tools.desc: Create a contract / agreement. Clauses = { id, title, content, required }. Signers = { name, email, role?, order? } — each gets a unique signing token. Starts in draft.

tools.name: contracts_get
tools.desc: Fetch contract + all signer records (name, email, status, signedAt).

tools.name: contracts_list
tools.desc: List contracts / agreements for the client. Filter by status or linked proposal.

tools.name: contracts_void
tools.desc: Mark a contract as voided (not executable). Stamps voidedAt + reason. Cannot be undone via MCP.

tools.name: crm_activities_create
tools.desc: Log an activity against a contact, deal, or company. Type "note" captures a plain observation; "task" supports dueDate; "completedAt" marks it done.

args.name: dueDate
args.desc: ISO datetime (for tasks).

args.name: completedAt
args.desc: ISO datetime — mark activity as complete.

tools.name: crm_activities_list
tools.desc: List logged activities (calls, emails, meetings, notes, tasks) filtered by contact/deal/company.

tools.name: crm_companies_create
tools.desc: Create a new CRM company.

tools.name: crm_companies_search
tools.desc: Search CRM companies by name or domain.

tools.name: crm_companies_update
tools.desc: Update any mutable field on a CRM company.

tools.name: crm_contacts_create
tools.desc: Create a new CRM contact.

tools.name: crm_contacts_search
tools.desc: Search CRM contacts by name or email.

tools.name: crm_contacts_update
tools.desc: Update any mutable field on a CRM contact. Pass null to clear nullable fields.

tools.name: crm_custom_field_values_get
tools.desc: Fetch custom field values (joined with their definitions) for a given contact, company, or deal.

tools.name: crm_custom_field_values_set
tools.desc: Set (insert or update) custom field values on a contact/company/deal. Pass values as { [fieldId]: stringValue }. Pass empty string or null to clear.

tools.name: crm_custom_fields_create
tools.desc: Define a custom field on contact/company/deal. For select/multiselect types, provide options[].

tools.name: crm_custom_fields_delete
tools.desc: Remove a custom field definition. All stored values for this field are cascaded.

tools.name: crm_custom_fields_list
tools.desc: List custom field definitions attached to contact/company/deal entities.

tools.name: crm_custom_fields_update
tools.desc: Rename, toggle required, reorder, or update options on an existing custom field definition.

tools.name: crm_deal_artifact_link
tools.desc: Attach a website, email campaign, pitch deck, proposal, booking, survey, or project to a CRM deal. The artifact must belong to this client.

tools.name: crm_deal_artifact_toggle_pin
tools.desc: Update the pinned flag on a linked deal artifact.

tools.name: crm_deal_artifact_unlink
tools.desc: Remove an artifact link from a deal. Deletes the link row; the underlying artifact is not touched.

tools.name: crm_deal_artifacts_list
tools.desc: List every artifact (website, email campaign, pitch deck, proposal, booking, survey, project) linked to a CRM deal.

tools.name: crm_deal_comments_create
tools.desc: Add a comment to a deal. Use @[name](userId) tokens for mentions — mentioned users get an in-app notification, scoped to members of the same client. The portal route's notification call was previously fire-and-forget; this handler awaits it so MCP-driven comments don't silently miss notifications.

args.name: parentCommentId
args.desc: Optional id of the root comment being replied to. Must belong to the same deal. One level of threading only.

args.name: mentionedUserIds
args.desc: Optional explicit list of user IDs to notify. Merged with any @[name](userId) tokens parsed from the body. Filtered to client members.

tools.name: crm_deal_comments_delete
tools.desc: Delete one of the caller's own comments on a deal. Matches the portal route — cannot delete other users' comments.

tools.name: crm_deal_comments_list
tools.desc: List comments (with author name and attachments) on a deal. Bodies may contain @[name](userId) mention tokens.

tools.name: crm_deals_create
tools.desc: Create a new deal in a pipeline stage.

args.name: value
args.desc: Amount in cents

tools.name: crm_deals_delete
tools.desc: Permanently delete a CRM deal. Cascades to deal artifacts and comments via FK ON DELETE CASCADE.

tools.name: crm_deals_get
tools.desc: Fetch a single deal with joined contact/company/stage display fields. Pass includeCustomFields=true to also receive the deal's custom-field map ({ [fieldId]: { name, type, value } }).

tools.name: crm_deals_list
tools.desc: List deals in a pipeline, or across all pipelines for the client.

tools.name: crm_deals_move_stage

tools.name: decks_publish_all
tools.desc: Walks every slide on a deck and publishes any that have a non-null `draft`. Removes `pendingDelete` tombstones, materializes `pendingCreate` slides, and merges regular update drafts into live fields. Use after a batch of `decks_replace_slides` / `decks_add_slide` calls to flip the whole deck live in one shot.

If the slide's draft has `pendingDelete: true` the slide is removed from the deck; if it has `pendingCreate: true` (or a regular update draft) the draft's `blocks/customCss/pageSettings/notes` are copied onto the live fields and `draft` is cleared. Use after `decks_replace_slides`, `decks_add_slide`, or `decks_upload_html` to make changes visible in the public renderer.

tools.name: decks_replace_slides
tools.desc: Replace the entire slide array of a deck with a new V2 slide list. Writes land in slide drafts — the public renderer keeps showing the previous live slides until you call `decks_publish_slide` or `decks_publish_all` to make them live. Existing slides that match by `id` get their `draft.{blocks,customCss,pageSettings,notes}` updated. New slide ids become slides with `draft.pendingCreate = true` and empty live fields. Existing slides missing from the incoming list become tombstones with `draft.pendingDelete = true` until publish. Each slide = { id, label, blocks[], notes?, pageSettings?, customCss? }. Blocks follow the visual-editor schema — you MUST read blocks://schema before calling this (it documents block `style`, `elementStyles`, and per-slide `customCss` used for polished slides). Rules: (1) use `heading` blocks with explicit `level` for titles — never a big `text` block; (2) pair every heading with a small uppercase eyebrow `text` block above it for branded feel; (3) if you use a hero block, populate title + subtitle + description + ctaText/ctaLink — a title-only hero looks broken; (4) apply `style` (color, fontSize, fontWeight, letterSpacing) to add visual hierarchy instead of relying on defaults. Returns the slim deck projection by default — pass `includeSlides: true` only if you need the slides echoed back (you just sent them, so usually you do not).

args.name: slug
args.desc: Derived from name if omitted.

tools.name: taxonomies_create_tag
tools.desc: Create a tag on a website. Slug must be unique per website.

tools.name: taxonomies_list
tools.desc: List categories and tags scoped to a website (the client must own it).

tools.name: team_invite
tools.desc: Invite a user to this client by email. If the email is unknown, creates a new user with a generated temp password (returned in the response). If the email exists, links them as a member without changing their password. Only the account owner may invite — non-owners get a permission error.

tools.name: team_list_members
tools.desc: List users with access to this client (via client_members). Returns user name, email, and role.

tools.name: team_remove_member
tools.desc: Remove a user's client_members row for this client. Does not delete the user account.

tools.name: team_update_role
tools.desc: Change a team member's role (owner/admin/member/viewer). Requires team:write. Demoting the last remaining owner is rejected server-side to avoid orphaning the account.

tools.name: tickets_attach_file_from_url
tools.desc: Download a remote file (http/https, 25 MB cap), upload it to S3, and post a new ticket message with the file attached. Optionally include a body.

args.name: body
args.desc: Message body to accompany the file; defaults to a note referencing the filename.

args.name: filename
args.desc: Override; defaults to URL basename.

tools.name: tickets_create
tools.desc: Open a new support ticket.

tools.name: tickets_get
tools.desc: Fetch a support ticket and its message thread.

tools.name: tickets_list
tools.desc: List support tickets for the client.

tools.name: tickets_reply
tools.desc: Append a message to a support ticket.

tools.name: tickets_update
tools.desc: Change ticket status, priority, category, or assignee. Setting status to "resolved" stamps resolvedAt.

args.name: assignedTo
args.desc: User id; pass null to unassign.

tools.name: usage_get
tools.desc: Return this client's own MCP tool-call and token-spend summary for the past N days (default 7, max 90). Covers totalCalls, totalErrors, errorRate, totalTokens, and estimated cost.

tools.name: website_domains_add
tools.desc: Add a custom domain to a website (starts pending until DNS verification). This does NOT provision DNS records — user must configure them externally.

tools.name: website_domains_list
tools.desc: List custom domains attached to a website.

tools.name: website_domains_remove
tools.desc: Remove a custom domain attachment. Does not affect external DNS.

tools.name: website_env_vars_delete
tools.desc: Remove an env var by id.

tools.name: website_env_vars_list
tools.desc: List env vars for a website environment (defaults to production). Values ARE included — treat output as secrets.

tools.name: website_env_vars_set
tools.desc: Upsert an env var on a website environment (production/staging). Marks syncedToVercel=false — actual Vercel sync happens via portal UI.

tools.name: whoami
tools.desc: Return the authenticated portal user and client context.
